rationale: C02 is a highly plausible direct drafting template. It reproduces the same lengthy statutory quotations from sections 9 and 1(e) of title 17, follows them with country-specific evidence of reciprocal copyright protection, and uses nearly the same operative declaration that the statutory conditions have been fulfilled and that the foreign country's nationals receive title 17 benefits subject to the same exception. C05 and C21 use the same machinery and much of the same language, but C02 is more recent and its formulation most closely matches the child's wording and structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of title 17 of the United States Code, entitled "Copyrights" ... provides in part that the copyright secured by such title shall extend to the work of an author or proprietor who is a citizen or subject of a foreign state or nation only
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of title 17 of the United States Code, entitled "Copyrights" ... provides in part that the copyright secured ... by the said title shall extend to the work of an author or proprietor who is a citizen of a foreign state or nation only
shared_material.explanation: Both begin with essentially the same statutory introduction and then reproduce the same subsections 9(a) and 9(b).

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 1 of the said title 17 provides in part as follows: Any person entitled thereto ... shall have the exclusive right ... (e) To perform the copyrighted work publicly for profit if it be a musical composition
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 1 of the said title 17 provides in part as follows: Any person entitled thereto ... shall have the exclusive right ... (e) To perform the copyrighted work publicly for profit if it be a musical composition
shared_material.explanation: The same lengthy section 1(e) quotation, including its mechanical-reproduction proviso, appears in the same position.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of the said title 17 further provides: The existence of the reciprocal conditions aforesaid shall be determined by the President ... by proclamation made from time to time
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of the said title 17 further provides: The existence of the reciprocal conditions aforesaid shall be determined by the President ... by proclamation made from time to time
shared_material.explanation: This identical presidential-determination clause supplies the same legal bridge to the operative proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the conditions specified in sections 9 (b) and 1 (e) ... have, as between the United States and India, existed and been fulfilled, and ... citizens of India ... are entitled to all the benefits ... except those ... regarding the extension of time for fulfilling copyright conditions and formalities
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the conditions specified in section 9 (b) and 1 (e) ... have existed and have been fulfilled with respect to the nationals of Japan, and ... nationals of Japan ... [are] entitled ... to all the benefits ... except those ... regarding the extension of time for fulfilling copyright conditions and formalities
shared_material.explanation: The operative provision is materially the same, with India and its relevant dates substituted for Japan and its dates.
